evidence: Cic. Off. 1.51 (Ennius): nihilō minus ipsī lūcet
Tib. 1.1.6: dum meus assiduō lūceat igne focus (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The plain word for anything that gives light: the sun, the moon, a lamp, a fire, eyes. Impersonal lūcet is “it is getting light, it is day” (Cic. Att. 6.2.10).

evidence: Cic. Cat. 2.5: quī nitent unguentīs, quī fulgent purpurā (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Properly of lightning (impersonal fulget, “it lightens”); then of what flashes or glitters: metal, purple, jewels.

terms.gloss: shine, gleam; look sleek and glossy
evidence: Lucr. 1.9: plācātumque nitet diffūsō lūmine caelum (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The shine of what is clear, clean, polished or well kept: a cloudless sky, bronze rubbed bright, a sleek animal; also of people and fields, to look well, to thrive (Lewis & Short).

terms.register: vōx plērumque poētica: Enn., Verg., Hor.
terms.comment: Lewis & Short calls it mostly poetic; Cicero has it once, figuratively: virtūs lūcet in tenebrīs splendetque per sēsē semper (Cic. Sest. 60).

phrases.latin: nihilō minus ipsī lūcet, cum illī accenderit
phrases.english: his own lamp shines no less when he has lit the other man’s

phrases.latin: cupiēbam etiam nunc plūra garrīre sed lūcet
phrases.english: I’d like to chatter on, but it’s getting light

phrases.latin: jamdūdum splendet focus et tibi munda supellex
phrases.english: the hearth has been glowing for ages, and the things on the table are clean and ready for you

phrases.latin: et nitet indūctō candida barba gelū
phrases.english: and a white beard shines with a coat of frost

sources: Lewis & Short: luceo · Lewis & Short: fulgeo · Lewis & Short: niteo · Lewis & Short: splendeo
